newsitem.title: UK: LucasVarity details reshape, disposals plan.
newsitem.headline: LucasVarity details reshape, disposals plan.

text.p: Anglo-U.S. auto components group LucasVarity Plc said on Tuesday it was planning to accelerate a planned programme of rationalisation and disposals following its creation through the merger of Britain's Lucas Industries and Varity Corp of the U.S. earlier this year.

In a statement, the company said it had identified a range of additional restructuring plans that meant it saw an extra 120 million pounds ($200.2 million) of operating profit benefits, in addition to those anticipated at the time of merger.

It also expects to take an extra one-off charge of 130 million pounds ($217 million), mainly in non-cash items, which will be charged along with 120 million pounds of costs already planned from the company's accounts for the current year.
A study of potential disposal candidates from among the many smaller companies in the merged group structure has identified 13 businesses due for divestment by the end of 1997, LV said.
These have combined annual turnover equivalent to about 270 million pounds, and together employ about 5,000 people. The company said it anticipated gaining "full value" in their sales.
"The costs include initiatives to increase productivity, eliminate duplicate facilities and activities, reduce overhead and introduce best practices," the company said in a statement.
As a result, world-wide headcount across the group will be cut by 3,000 over the next two years, it added. ($1=.5995 Pound)
